- Overestimate prices in the short term after positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot early in the forecast horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment turns negative or shows strong bearish signals (e.g., sentiment < 0.06 or multiple consecutive negative values).
- Reduce forecast magnitude by 5–10% if recent sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., -0.22 or -0.61) or if true outcome has dropped sharply from prior period.
- Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 10–15% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment shifts; if sentiment changes by >0.15 from prior day, adjust forecast only if confirmed by 2+ consecutive days of similar sentiment.
- For 30-day forecasts, reduce peak values if sentiment shows early signs of cooling (e.g., sentiment drops below 0.11 after a spike).
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast for 3–5 days, reduce next forecast by 5–8% to avoid “over-optimistic” bias.
- Do not assume sentiment directly translates to price; if sentiment is positive but price drops, reduce forecast by 3–5% to account for market volatility.
